open_items: ILO gateway_issue (cycle 1354): fresh occurrence of the catalogued Cloudflare/WAF 403 pattern on sdmx.ilo.org, affecting the listing-style gateway check (auth:listing, constraint:availableconstraint, errors:missing_artefact, references:contentconstraint, encoding:structure_xml) while direct metadata/data/json and six other contract reference checks stayed healthy. Not a blanket block this time. Watch next run: should self-clear within 1-3 cycles per history; escalate if it widens to the direct path or persists past 4 cycles.

STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 1354 (/api/contracts changes array has no new was/now pair for it this cycle, it just remains in that state). Still open, not re-reported since no new change.
claude/ triage branches on origin: 161 as of this run (160 last run), still well above the 20 the skill flags for pruning; not actioned by this read-only routine.

Monitor bug noted previously: /api/history computes status without contracts, so a contract-only degraded state never shows up in /api/history, only in /api/status and /api/contracts. Not re-verified this run since the contract-row breaks tracked a gateway-check status change this time.

Chronic gateway bug (empty 'Error: ' message from tools/sdmx_tools.py around lines 207-209 catching Exception with an empty str(e)): previously traced on ABS (many occurrences), ESTAT (cycle 1143, 1335), and ECB (cycle 1337, 1339-adjacent, 1345). Not fixed by this routine; it only commits to docs/monitor/. Not observed this run (the ILO failure carried its own explicit 403 error text, not an empty one).

Long-running architectural facts, not incidents: ILO /availableconstraint/ returns 500 (constraints come via ?references=all) -- this cycle it returned 403 instead of 500 purely because of the WAF block, tracked as part of the same ILO incident above, not a separate fact change; ECB does not support /availableconstraint/ (404 is expected, not an error); ESTAT has no practical constraint support; ESTAT direct json check is skipped by design (Eurostat returns 406 for SDMx-JSON); IMF direct json check is skipped by design (IMF ignores the JSON Accept header and returns XML); STATSNZ direct json check is skipped by design (Stats NZ ignores the JSON Accept header and returns CSV); BIS/IMF references:contentconstraint reads ignored (accepted and silently dropped, seen again this run); encoding:structure_xml Content-Type charset/version parameter order flips cosmetically from time to time across ABS/FBOS/ILO/SBS/OECD, verdict stays ok as always (seen again this run on ABS).
